claim: The COVID-19 pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2 infection has resulted in at least 755 million diagnosed cases and over 6.8 million deaths.
source: The COVID-19 pandemic caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection has spread globally, with at least 755 million people diagnosed and the death toll is over 6.8 million.
evidence: These are stated statistics about the pandemic's impact.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern, including Alpha, Beta, Delta, and Omicron, continue to evolve and increase transmissibility and the ability to escape host immune responses.
source: SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern, including Alpha, Beta, Delta, and Omicron, continue to evolve and increase transmissibility and the ability to escape host immune responses.
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to Zhou et al., 2020 and represents established knowledge about viral evolution.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 infection induces cell-cell fusion (syncytia formation) in multiple cell types including lung epithelial cells, neurons, and glia.
source: SARS-CoV-2 infection induces cell-cell fusion (also known as syncytia formation) in multiple cell types including lung epithelial cells, neurons, and glia (Martínez-Mármol et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Martínez-Mármol et al., 2023.

claim: Syncytia formation between SARS-CoV-2-infected cells with neighboring cells may contribute to increased viral transmission and pathogenicity in the infected host.
source: Syncytia formation between SARS-CoV-2-infected cells with neighboring cells may contribute to increased viral transmission and pathogenicity in the infected host (Rajah et al., 2022), which also makes the virus insensitive to extracellular neutralizing antibodies (Li et al., 2022; Yu et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rajah et al., 2022, Li et al., 2022, and Yu et al., 2023.

claim: Syncytia formation makes the virus insensitive to extracellular neutralizing antibodies.
source: Syncytia formation between SARS-CoV-2-infected cells with neighboring cells may contribute to increased viral transmission and pathogenicity in the infected host (Rajah et al., 2022), which also makes the virus insensitive to extracellular neutralizing antibodies (Li et al., 2022; Yu et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2022 and Yu et al., 2023.

claim: Syncytia formation among pneumocytes with long-term persistence of viral RNA has been observed in the lung autopsy of deceased COVID-19 donors.
source: Moreover, syncytia formation among pneumocytes with long-term persistence of viral RNA has been observed in the lung autopsy of deceased COVID-19 donors, which may contribute to prolonged clearance of the virus and long COVID symptoms (Bussani et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bussani et al., 2020.

claim: SARS-CoV-2-mediated syncytia formation is effectively inhibited by multiple interferon (IFN)-stimulating genes (ISGs).
source: It has been reported that SARS-CoV-2-mediated syncytia formation is effectively inhibited by multiple interferon (IFN)-stimulating genes (ISGs) (Pfaender et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pfaender et al., 2020 and Wang et al., 2020.

claim: Low IFN levels with impaired ISG responses were observed during early SARS-CoV-2 infection in severe COVID-19 patients.
source: However, low IFN levels with impaired ISG responses were observed during early SARS-CoV-2 infection, which may have compromised the antiviral responses of IFN in severe COVID-19 patients (Blanco-Melo et al., 2020; Hadjadj et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blanco-Melo et al., 2020 and Hadjadj et al., 2020.

claim: Cell culture supernatants of THP-1 cells stimulated by TLR ligands significantly reduced the bioluminescence signal in SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion assays.
source: Of note, cell culture supernatants of THP-1 cells stimulated by TLR ligands significantly reduced the bioluminescence signal, while neither untreated THP-1 cell culture supernatant nor the medium control had any effect on the bioluminescence signal reflecting cell-cell fusion (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TLR ligands-stimulated THP-1 cell culture supernatants clearly reduced S2' cleavage in HEK293T-Spike and HEK293T-ACE2 co-cultures.
source: In parallel with bioluminescence assay, a large amount of enriched S2' cleavage was detected in HEK293T-Spike and HEK293T-ACE2 co-cultured group and co-culture incubated with untreated THP-1 cell culture supernatant, while S2' cleavage was clearly reduced upon treatment with TLR ligands-stimulated THP-1 cell culture supernatants (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The area of syncytium was significantly reduced by treatment with TLR ligands-stimulated THP-1 cell culture supernatants.
source: Syncytia formation was also visualized using cells co-expressing spike and a ZsGreen fluorescent reporter. The area of syncytium were significantly reduced by the treatment with TLR ligands-stimulated THP-1 cell culture supernatants (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TLR ligands alone did not reduce the bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage compared to the control groups.
source: As expected, TLR ligands alone did not reduce the bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage compared to the control groups, as well as no effect on syncytia formation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E.

claim: TLR ligands-stimulated PBMCs culture supernatants treatment strongly reduced the bioluminescence signal, S2' cleavage, and the area of syncytium.
source: Consistent with the results from THP-1 cells, TLR ligands-stimulated PBMCs culture supernatants treatment also strongly reduced the bioluminescence signal, S2' cleavage, and the area of syncytium compared with the medium group (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–I.

claim: TLR ligands-stimulated-THP-1 cell culture supernatants reduced S2' cleavage and N protein levels during Delta or WT SARS-CoV-2 infection in HEK293T-ACE2 cells.
source: Result from this experiment showed that TLR ligands-stimulated-THP-1 cell culture supernatants reduced S2' cleavage and N protein levels during Delta or WT SARS-CoV-2 infection in HEK293T-ACE2 cells, whereas untreated THP-1 cell culture supernatant had no effect (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: TLR ligands-stimulated THP-1 cell culture supernatants significantly reduced the area of syncytium during SARS-CoV-2 infection in Caco-2 cells.
source: Accordingly, immunofluorescent staining also showed that TLR ligands-stimulated THP-1 cell culture supernatants significantly reduced the area of syncytium during SARS-CoV-2 infection in Caco-2 cells (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: The expression levels of IL1A, IL1B, IL6, and IL8 were significantly increased upon TLR ligands stimulation in THP-1 cells.
source: It was found that the expression levels of IL1A, IL1B, IL6, and IL8 were significantly increased upon TLR ligands stimulation, while IL4, IL12A, IFNA1, IFNB1, and IFNG mRNA levels were not changed or undetected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: IL-1α and IL-1β significantly reduced the bioluminescence signal compared to the control group in SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion assays.
source: Interestingly, IL-1α and IL-1β significantly reduced the bioluminescence signal compared to the control group, while IL-6 and IL-8 had little or no effect (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: IL-1α and IL-1β significantly inhibited SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced syncytia formation.
source: In addition, fluorescence images of cells expressing ZsGreen reporter also confirmed that IL-1α and IL-1β significantly inhibited SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced syncytia formation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: When both IL-1α and IL-1β were added, there was no synergistic inhibition on cell-cell fusion compared to either cytokine alone.
source: Intriguingly, when we added both IL-1α and IL-1β, there was no synergistic inhibition on cell-cell fusion compared to either cytokine alone (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–H), suggesting a saturation of IL-1 receptor binding to these homologues.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–H and includes an inference about receptor saturation.

claim: IL-1β reduced S2' cleavage and N protein levels compared to the control group during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection in HEK293T-ACE2 and Caco-2 cells.
source: To this end, it was found that IL-1β reduced S2' cleavage and N protein levels compared to the control group during such infection both in HEK293T-ACE2 (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A) and in Caco-2 cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F, G, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: IL-1β inhibited authentic SARS-CoV-2-induced syncytia formation.
source: Meanwhile, IL-1β inhibited authentic SARS-CoV-2-induced syncytia formation (Figure 2H and I and Figure 2—figure supplement 3B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H, I, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3B and C.

claim: Innate immune cells activated by TLR ligands secreted IL-1β into the cell culture supernatants.
source: As expected, innate immune cells activated by TLR ligands secreted IL-1β into the cell culture supernatants (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and B.

claim: IL-1RA treatment reduced the inhibitory effect of PGN-stimulated-THP-1 cell culture supernatant on cell-cell fusion.
source: We employed IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA) to block IL-1 receptor on target cells, and found that IL-1RA treatment reduced the inhibitory effect of PGN-stimulated-THP-1 cell culture supernatant on cell-cell fusion (Figure 2J and Figure 2—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J and Figure 2—figure supplement 4C.

claim: TLR2 was essential for THP-1 cells to release IL-1β in response to TLR2 ligands.
source: With another note, TLR2 was essential for THP-1 cells to release IL-1β in response to TLR2 ligands (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4D.

claim: The cell culture supernatants of TLR2-knockout THP-1 cells stimulated by TLR2 ligands had no effect on the bioluminescence signal.
source: More importantly, the cell culture supernatants of TLR2-knockout THP-1 cells stimulated by TLR2 ligands had no effect on the bioluminescence signal, while the cell culture supernatants from WT THP-1 cells stimulated by the same TLR2 Ligands significantly reduced the bioluminescence signal (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4E.

claim: Pre-treatment with TAK1 inhibitor (5Z-7) or IKKβ inhibitor (TPCA1) in WT THP-1 cells prevented IL-1β secretion after PGN stimulation.
source: In addition, pre-treatment with TAK1 inhibitor (5Z-7) or IKKβ inhibitor (TPCA1) in WT THP-1 cells prevented IL-1β secretion after PGN stimulation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4F), as well as eliminated the inhibitory effect of PGN-stimulated WT THP-1 cell culture supernatant on SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion (Figure 2—figure supplement 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4F and G.

claim: Pre-treatment of either HEK293T-S or HEK293T-ACE2 cells with IL-1β alone reduced bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage.
source: Notably, pre-treatment of either HEK293T-S or HEK293T-ACE2 cells with IL-1β alone reduced bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage; when IL-1β pre-treatment on both HEK293T-S and HEK293T-ACE2 cells was applied, bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage were further reduced (Figure 2—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5B.

claim: IL-1β reduced the bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in different SARS-CoV-2 variants.
source: Notably, IL-1β reduced the bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in different SARS-CoV-2 variants (Figure 2—figure supplement 6C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6C–E.

claim: IL-1β also reduced bioluminescence signal, S2' cleavage, and the area of syncytium in SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV spike-induced cell-cell fusion systems.
source: Similar to SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion, IL-1β also reduced bioluminescence signal (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B and C), S2' cleavage (Figure 2—figure supplement 7D and E), and the area of syncytium (Figure 2—figure supplement 7F and G) in these cell-cell fusion systems.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7B–G.

claim: In the presence of IL-1RA, IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage.
source: First of all, in the presence of IL-1RA, IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In MyD88 knockout HEK293T cell line, IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage.
source: Next, as MyD88 is the downstream adaptor for IL-1R1, we generated MyD88 knockout HEK293T cell line, wherein IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal (Figure 3C) and S2' cleavage (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In the presence of IRAK1/4 inhibitor, IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage.
source: In addition, we found that IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in the presence of IRAK1/4 inhibitor (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In TRAF6 knockout HEK293T cell line, IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage.
source: Furthermore, IL-1β was unable to reduce bioluminescence signal (Figure 3E) and S2' cleavage (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) in TRAF6 knockout HEK293T cell line.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: IL-1β inhibits SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion through IL-1R1-MyD88-IRAK-TRAF6 pathway.
source: These results suggested that IL-1β inhibits SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion through IL-1R1-MyD88-IRAK-TRAF6 pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing the requirement of these pathway components.

claim: IL-1β still reduced bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in TAK1 knockout (sgMAP3K7) HEK293T cell line.
source: Intriguingly, when we tested TAK1, a downstream molecule of TRAF6 for the potential involvement in the signaling, it was found that IL-1β still reduced bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in TAK1 knockout (sgMAP3K7) HEK293T cell line (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In the presence of TPCA1, an IKKβ inhibitor, IL-1β still inhibited bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage.
source: Moreover, we found that in the presence of TPCA1, an IKKβ inhibitor, IL-1β still inhibited bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage as well (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: IL-1β still reduced the bioluminescence signal after NF-κB pathway-related genes knockout.
source: In addition, although IL-1β upregulated the mRNA transcription levels of NF-κB pathway-related genes, such as RELB, NFKBIA, and NFKB1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), IL-1β still reduced the bioluminescence signal after these NF-κB pathway-related genes knockout (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: IL-1β inhibits SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion independent from the TAK1-IKKβ-NF-κB signaling cascade.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated that IL-1β inhibits SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced cell-cell fusion independent from the TAK1-IKKβ-NF-κB signaling cascade.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing IL-1β activity persists despite blocking this pathway.

claim: IL-1β failed to reduce S2' cleavage and N protein levels in the presence of IRAK1/4 inhibitor in authentic SARS-CoV-2-infected Caco-2 and Calu-3 cells.
source: Consist with the results from HEK293T cells, IL-1β failed to reduce S2' cleavage and N protein levels in the presence of IRAK1/4 inhibitor, whereas it still reduced S2' cleavage and N protein amounts in the presence of the IKKβ inhibitor TPCA1 in Caco-2 (Figure 3F) and Calu-3 cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: IL-1β activated RhoA signaling in sgControl HEK293T cells but not in sgMyD88- or sgTRAF6-HEK293T cells.
source: To this end, we verified that IL-1β activated RhoA signaling in sgControl HEK293T cells but not in sgMyD88- or sgTRAF6-HEK293T cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: IL-1β significantly increased the fluorescence intensity of GFP-AHPH in sgControl HEK293T cells, but had no effect in sgMyD88- and sgTRAF6-HEK293T cells.
source: Interestingly, IL-1β significantly increased the fluorescence intensity of GFP-AHPH in sgControl HEK293T cells, but had no effect in sgMyD88- and sgTRAF6-HEK293T cells (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: In the process of syncytia formation without IL-1β treatment, GFP-AHPH localized distally from cell-cell junction in the early stage and at the periphery of syncytium with enlargement.
source: In the process of syncytia formation, cell-cell contact established between S-expressing cells and ACE2-expressing cells, and GFP-AHPH localized distally from cell-cell junction in the early stage of syncytia formation. With the enlargement of syncytium, GFP-AHPH is visualized at the periphery of syncytium (Figure 4D, top panel, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D (top panel) and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In IL-1β-treated group, GFP-AHPH foci is enriched to the cell-cell junction in the early stage and recruited more to the cell-cell junction over time, preventing further cell-cell fusion.
source: However, in IL-1β-treated group, GFP-AHPH foci is enriched to the cell-cell junction in the early stage. Over time, GFP-AHPH was recruited more to the cell-cell junction between S-expressing cells and ACE2-expressing cells, preventing further cell-cell fusion (Figure 4D, bottom panel, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D (bottom panel) and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Constitutive activation of RhoA enriches actin filaments (F-actin) at cell-cell junction and clearly reduces the bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in a dose-dependent manner.
source: We co-transfected constitutively activated RhoA L63 (Nobes and Hall, 1999) (RhoA-CA) plasmid with spike or ACE2 in HEK293T cells, and found that constitutive activation of RhoA enriches actin filaments (F-actin) at cell-cell junction (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A) and clearly reduces the bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, with citation to Nobes and Hall, 1999.

claim: F-actin at cell-cell junction between S-expressing cells and ACE2-expressing cells was gradually disappeared along with cell-cell fusion in the early stages of syncytia formation without IL-1β treatment.
source: Moreover, we observed that F-actin at cell-cell junction between S-expressing cells and ACE2-expressing cells was gradually disappeared along with cell-cell fusion in the early stages of syncytia formation. With the formation and enlargement of syncytium, F-actin of syncytium is preferably distributed peripherally (Figure 4F, top panel, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F (top panel) and Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: IL-1β activated RhoA to initiate actin bundles formation at cell-cell junction, which prevents membrane fusion between S-expressing cells and ACE2-expressing cells.
source: However, IL-1β activated RhoA to initiate actin bundles formation at cell-cell junction, the formation of these actin bundles potentially generates barriers and prevents membrane fusion between S-expressing cells and ACE2-expressing cells. Even with the prolonged co-culture time, IL-1β-induced actin bundles formed at cell junctions consistently inhibited further syncytia formation (Figure 4F, middle panel, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F (middle panel) and Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 treatment prevented the formation of IL-1β-induced actin bundles at cell-cell junctions, thus promoted membrane fusion and restored syncytia formation.
source: Of note, ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 prevents the formation of actin bundles (van der Heijden et al., 2008; Watanabe et al., 1999). Here, we found that the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 treatment prevented the formation of IL-1β-induced actin bundles at cell-cell junctions, thus promoted membrane fusion and cytoplasmic exchange between S-expressing cells and ACE2-expressing cells and restored syncytia formation (Figure 4F, bottom panel, and Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F (bottom panel) and Figure 4—figure supplement 3A, with citations to van der Heijden et al., 2008 and Watanabe et al., 1999.

claim: Upon authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection, GFP-AHPH moved to the opposite of cell-cell junction and located peripherally with syncytia formation.
source: Importantly, upon authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection, we observed consistent results: immunofluorescence (IF) staining showed GFP-AHPH moving to the opposite of cell-cell junction and located peripherally with syncytia formation (Figure 5A, top panel, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), while upon IL-1β treatment, GFP-AHPH located to the cell-cell junction of infected cells and neighboring cells (Figure 5A, bottom panel, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A (top panel) and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Upon IL-1β treatment during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection, GFP-AHPH located to the cell-cell junction of infected cells and neighboring cells.
source: Importantly, upon authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection, we observed consistent results: immunofluorescence (IF) staining showed GFP-AHPH moving to the opposite of cell-cell junction and located peripherally with syncytia formation (Figure 5A, top panel, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), while upon IL-1β treatment, GFP-AHPH located to the cell-cell junction of infected cells and neighboring cells (Figure 5A, bottom panel, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A (bottom panel) and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: F-actin at the cell-cell junction were disassembled during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection, and with the formation of syncytium, F-actin was mainly distributed peripherally.
source: In parallel, staining results showed that F-actin at the cell-cell junction were disassembled during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection; with the formation of syncytium, F-actin was mainly distributed peripherally. However, actin bundles formed at cell-cell junction upon IL-1β inhibition of membrane fusion and further syncytia formation (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: Actin bundles formed at cell-cell junction upon IL-1β inhibition of membrane fusion and further syncytia formation during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: In parallel, staining results showed that F-actin at the cell-cell junction were disassembled during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection; with the formation of syncytium, F-actin was mainly distributed peripherally. However, actin bundles formed at cell-cell junction upon IL-1β inhibition of membrane fusion and further syncytia formation (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: HEK293T-ACE2, Caco-2, and Calu-3 cells expressing RhoA-CA clearly reduced S2' cleavage and N protein levels compared to the control group during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: To further investigate the role of RhoA/ROCK pathway in inhibiting SARS-CoV-2 induced cell-cell fusion, we found that HEK293T-ACE2 (Figure 5C), Caco-2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), and Calu-3 cells (Figure 5D) expressing RhoA-CA clearly reduced S2' cleavage and N protein levels compared to the control group during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, D, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Constitutive activation of RhoA enriches actin bundles at cell-cell junction, thus preventing SARS-CoV-2-induced cell-cell fusion in authentic SARS-CoV-2 infected Caco-2 and Calu-3 cells.
source: Meanwhile, we observed that constitutive activation of RhoA enriches actin bundles at cell-cell junction, thus preventing SARS-CoV-2-induced cell-cell fusion in authentic SARS-CoV-2 infected Caco-2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C) and Calu-3 cells (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B, C, and D.

claim: RhoA-CA did not affect Spike protein binding to ACE2.
source: In addition, we examined the potential effect of RhoA-CA on ACE2 and found that it did not affect Spike protein binding to ACE2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E), nor ACE2 distribution on the cell surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2E.

claim: RhoA-CA did not affect ACE2 distribution on the cell surface.
source: In addition, we examined the potential effect of RhoA-CA on ACE2 and found that it did not affect Spike protein binding to ACE2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E), nor ACE2 distribution on the cell surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2F and G.

claim: IL-1β treatment did not change ACE2 or Spike protein distribution on the cell surface.
source: We also observed that IL-1β treatment did not change ACE2 or Spike protein distribution on the cell surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A–D.

claim: ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 treatment increased bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in a dose-dependent manner, promoting syncytia formation.
source: Notably, ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 treatment increased bioluminescence signal and S2' cleavage in a dose-dependent manner, promoting syncytia formation. When treated with lower concentrations of Y-27632, IL-1β eliminated Y-27632-enhanced cell-cell fusion. However, IL-1β was unable to inhibit cell-cell fusion in the presence of higher concentrations of Y-27632 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3E.

claim: IL-1β was unable to reduce S2' cleavage and N protein levels in the presence of Y-27632 in authentic SARS-CoV-2-infected Caco-2, Calu-3 cells, and primary human lung cells.
source: Furthermore, we verified that IL-1β was unable to reduce S2' cleavage and N protein levels in the presence of Y-27632 in authentic SARS-CoV-2-infected Caco-2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F), Calu-3 cells (Figure 5F), and primary human lung cells (Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F, G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 3F.

claim: Y-27632 eliminated IL-1β induced actin bundles in Caco-2 and Calu-3 cells during authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: IF results also confirmed that the elimination of IL-1β induced actin bundles by Y-27632 in Caco-2 (Figure 5—figure supplements 3G and 4A) and Calu-3 cells (Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H, Figure 5—figure supplements 3G, 4A, and 4B.

claim: In mice with IL-1β treatment, the body weight loss was less than in the PBS control group during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: Interestingly, the results of this experiment showed that in mice with IL-1β treatment, the body weight loss was less than in the PBS control group, while IL-1β was unable to improve body weight in the presence of IL-1RA (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: IL-1β was unable to improve body weight in the presence of IL-1RA during SARS-CoV-2 infection in mice.
source: Interestingly, the results of this experiment showed that in mice with IL-1β treatment, the body weight loss was less than in the PBS control group, while IL-1β was unable to improve body weight in the presence of IL-1RA (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Mice with IL-1β treatment carry less pulmonary injury compared to the PBS control and IL-1RA+IL-1β groups during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: According to hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, tissue histopathology analysis demonstrated that the mice with IL-1β treatment carry less pulmonary injury compared to the PBS control and IL-1RA+IL-1β groups (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: The expression level of SARS-CoV-2 N gene in the lung from IL-1β-treated mice was significantly lower than in the PBS control and IL-1RA+IL-1β-treated mice.
source: In addition, the expression level of SARS-CoV-2 N gene in the lung from IL-1β-treated mice was significantly lower than in the PBS control and IL-1RA+IL-1β-treated mice (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The infected area in the epithelial linings of lung tissue was significantly reduced by IL-1β treatment compared to the PBS control and IL-1RA+IL-1β groups.
source: In addition, immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining showed that the infected area in the epithelial linings of lung tissue was significantly reduced by IL-1β treatment compared to the PBS control and IL-1RA+IL-1β groups (Figure 6D and E), indicating that IL-1β restricted the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in the lung.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: IL-1β restricted the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in the lung.
source: In addition, immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining showed that the infected area in the epithelial linings of lung tissue was significantly reduced by IL-1β treatment compared to the PBS control and IL-1RA+IL-1β groups (Figure 6D and E), indicating that IL-1β restricted the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in the lung.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing reduced infected area.

claim: IL-1β induced the formation of actin bundles to restrict the syncytia formation and further viral transmission in SARS-CoV-2-infected lung epithelial cells in vivo.
source: Moreover, fluorescence staining showed that SARS-CoV-2-infected lung epithelial cells fused with neighboring cells, promoting viral transmission in the airway epithelial cells, while IL-1β induced the formation of actin bundles to restrict the syncytia formation and further viral transmission (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: IL-1β-treated mice have no significant changes in body weight, nor liver and spleen weight compared to control mice.
source: In addition, we found that IL-1β-treated mice have no significant changes in body weight, nor liver and spleen weight compared to control mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–D), indicating that this dose of IL-1β did not cause toxicity in vivo in the mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: S2' cleavage and N protein levels were strongly reduced in IL-1β-treated mice-derived lung and intestine tissue cells compared to control when infected with authentic SARS-CoV-2.
source: Of note, when we isolated tissue cells from the IL-1β-treated mice and infected with authentic SARS-CoV-2, it was found that S2' cleavage and N protein levels were strongly reduced in IL-1β-treated mice-derived lung and intestine tissue cells compared to control (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2E), suggesting that IL-1β may have protective effects on various tissue cells against SARS-CoV-2 infection in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Y-27632 compromised the effect of IL-1β in preventing weight loss during SARS-CoV-2 infection in mice.
source: Similar to IL-1RA, Y-27632 compromised the effect of IL-1β in preventing weight loss (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Y-27632 treatment aggravated lung injury in IL-1β-treated mice upon SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: In addition, H&E staining showed that Y-27632 treatment aggravated lung injury in IL-1β-treated mice upon SARS-CoV-2 infection (Figure 7A and B), although Y-27632+IL-1β did not cause weight loss or lung injury in uninfected mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Y-27632 treatment increased the expression level of SARS-CoV-2 N gene and infected area in the lungs of IL-1β-treated mice.
source: Moreover, Y-27632 treatment increased the expression level of SARS-CoV-2 N gene (Figure 7C) and infected area (Figure 7D and E) in the lungs of IL-1β-treated mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C, D, and E.

claim: Y-27632 treatment prevented the formation of IL-1β-induced actin bundles at cell-cell junctions, thus promoted syncytia formation and further viral transmission in vivo.
source: Importantly, Y-27632 treatment prevented the formation of IL-1β-induced actin bundles at cell-cell junctions, thus promoted syncytia formation and further viral transmission (Figure 7F and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: S2' cleavage and N protein levels were clearly reduced in IL-1β-treated mice compared to control at day 2, while Y-27632 treatment abolished the inhibitory effect of IL-1β.
source: Here, it was found that S2' cleavage and N protein levels were clearly reduced in IL-1β-treated mice compared to control at day 2, while Y-27632 treatment abolished the inhibitory effect of IL-1β (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The lung tissue cells in IL-1β-treated mice remained resistant to SARS-CoV-2 infection at day 7, while the protective effect of IL-1β was abolished by Y-27632 treatment.
source: Of note, the lung tissue cells in IL-1β-treated mice remained resistant to SARS-CoV-2 infection at day 7, while the protective effect of IL-1β was abolished by Y-27632 treatment (Figure 7G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: IL-1β prevents the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 through inducing the formation of actin bundles via the RhoA/ROCK pathway in vivo.
source: Taken together, IL-1β prevents the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 through inducing the formation of actin bundles via the RhoA/ROCK pathway in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing the mechanism of IL-1β action in vivo.

claim: IL-1β is a key mediator of inflammation.
source: Through cytokine screening, we identified that interleukin-1β (IL-1β), a key mediator of inflammation, inhibits syncytia formation mediated by various SARS-CoV-2 strains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IL-1β's role in inflammation.

claim: IL-1β inhibits syncytia formation mediated by various SARS-CoV-2 strains.
source: Through cytokine screening, we identified that interleukin-1β (IL-1β), a key mediator of inflammation, inhibits syncytia formation mediated by various SARS-CoV-2 strains.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: IL-1β activates RhoA/ROCK signaling through a non-canonical IL-1 receptor-dependent pathway.
source: Mechanistically, IL-1β activates RhoA/ROCK signaling through a non-canonical IL-1 receptor-dependent pathway, which drives the enrichment of actin bundles at the cell-cell junctions, thus prevents syncytia formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data showing the signaling pathway.

claim: IL-1β drives the enrichment of actin bundles at the cell-cell junctions.
source: Mechanistically, IL-1β activates RhoA/ROCK signaling through a non-canonical IL-1 receptor-dependent pathway, which drives the enrichment of actin bundles at the cell-cell junctions, thus prevents syncytia formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data showing actin bundle formation.

claim: In vivo infection experiments in mice confirmed that IL-1β significantly restricted SARS-CoV-2 spread in the lung epithelium.
source: Notably, in vivo infection experiments in mice confirmed that IL-1β significantly restricted SARS-CoV-2 spread in the lung epithelium.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Elevated IL-1β levels in severe COVID-19 patients is central to innate immune response as it induces the expression of other proinflammatory cytokines.
source: Elevated IL-1β levels in severe COVID-19 patients is central to innate immune response as it induces the expression of other proinflammatory cytokines (Tahtinen et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tahtinen et al., 2022.

claim: IL-1α is also secreted during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: In addition, IL-1α is also secreted during SARS-CoV-2 infection (Xiao et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Xiao et al., 2021.

claim: Anakinra improved clinical outcomes and reduced mortality in severe COVID-19 patients.
source: Intriguingly, although anakinra, a recombinant human IL-1RA, improved clinical outcomes and reduced mortality in severe COVID-19 patients (Cavalli et al., 2020), it did not reduce mortality in mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients, and even increased the probability of serious adverse events (Tharaux et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cavalli et al., 2020.

claim: Anakinra did not reduce mortality in mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients, and even increased the probability of serious adverse events.
source: Intriguingly, although anakinra, a recombinant human IL-1RA, improved clinical outcomes and reduced mortality in severe COVID-19 patients (Cavalli et al., 2020), it did not reduce mortality in mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients, and even increased the probability of serious adverse events (Tharaux et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tharaux et al., 2021.

claim: IL-1 blockade significantly decreased the neutralizing activity of serous anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies in severe COVID-19 patients.
source: With another note, IL-1 blockade significantly decreased the neutralizing activity of serous anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies in severe COVID-19 patients (Della-Torre et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Della-Torre et al., 2021.

claim: IL-1β plays a key role in triggering vaccine-induced innate immunity.
source: Notably, IL-1β plays a key role in triggering vaccine-induced innate immunity, suggesting that innate immune responses play important roles in the antiviral defense by enhancing the protective efficacy of vaccines (Eisenbarth et al., 2008; Tahtinen et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Eisenbarth et al., 2008 and Tahtinen et al., 2022.

claim: Vaccination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) has been reported to confer nonspecific protection against heterologous pathogens, including protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection in humans and mice.
source: In addition, vaccination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) has been reported to confer nonspecific protection against heterologous pathogens, including protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection in humans and mice (Hilligan et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2024; Rivas et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hilligan et al., 2022, Lee et al., 2024, and Rivas et al., 2021.

claim: Lipid nanoparticle in mRNA vaccine and penton base in adenovirus vaccine can both activate innate immune cells to amplify the protective effect of vaccines.
source: Moreover, lipid nanoparticle in mRNA vaccine (Han et al., 2023) and penton base in adenovirus vaccine (Di Paolo et al., 2009) can both activate innate immune cells to amplify the protective effect of vaccines, which may also be attributed to IL-1β-mediated inhibition of SARS-CoV-2-induced cell-cell fusion on top of adaptive immune responses induced by the vaccines.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Han et al., 2023 and Di Paolo et al., 2009, with speculation about IL-1β's role.

claim: Patients with inherited MyD88 or IRAK4 deficiency have been reported to be selectively vulnerable to COVID-19 pneumonia.
source: With another note, patients with inherited MyD88 or IRAK4 deficiency have been reported to be selectively vulnerable to COVID-19 pneumonia. It was found that these patients' susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 can be attributed to impaired type I IFN production, which do not sense the virus correctly in the absence of MyD88 or IRAK4 (García-García et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to García-García et al., 2023.

claim: MyD88 signaling was essential for BCG-induced innate and type 1 helper T cell (TH1 cell) responses and protection against SARS-CoV-2.
source: Moreover, MyD88 signaling was essential for BCG-induced innate and type 1 helper T cell (TH1 cell) responses and protection against SARS-CoV-2, which is consistent with our fundings.
evidence: This claim is stated as consistent with the study's findings.

claim: Inactivation of RhoA/ROCK signaling is crucial for myoblast fusion.
source: For example, myoblast fusion is the key process of skeletal muscle terminal differentiation, inactivation of RhoA/ROCK signaling is crucial for myoblast fusion (Nishiyama et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nishiyama et al., 2004.

claim: The dissolution of F-actin focus is essential for cell-cell fusion.
source: Cell-cell fusion is mediated by actin cytoskeletal rearrangements, the dissolution of F-actin focus is essential for cell-cell fusion; in contrast, syncytia formation cannot proceed if disassembly of actin filaments or bundles is prevented (Doherty et al., 2011; Rodríguez-Pérez et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Doherty et al., 2011 and Rodríguez-Pérez et al., 2021.

claim: Syncytia formation cannot proceed if disassembly of actin filaments or bundles is prevented.
source: Cell-cell fusion is mediated by actin cytoskeletal rearrangements, the dissolution of F-actin focus is essential for cell-cell fusion; in contrast, syncytia formation cannot proceed if disassembly of actin filaments or bundles is prevented (Doherty et al., 2011; Rodríguez-Pérez et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Doherty et al., 2011 and Rodríguez-Pérez et al., 2021.

claim: When corticosteroids were applied to suppress the inflammatory response in patients infected by SARS-CoV or MERS-CoV, the clearance of viral RNA was obviously delayed.
source: In addition, when corticosteroids were applied to suppress the inflammatory response in patients infected by SARS-CoV (Lee et al., 2004) or MERS-CoV (Arabi et al., 2018), the clearance of viral RNA was obviously delayed, suggesting the importance of innate immune factors in viral clearance.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2004 and Arabi et al., 2018.
